hooks.text: A federal law banned Chinese astronauts from the ISS.
A ban from the International Space Station built a new one.
One law forced China to build its own space station.

title: How a Space Ban Created a New Station
description: When US law barred Chinese astronauts from the International Space Station, China responded by building its own modular outpost and a telescope that dwarfs Hubble.

beats.text: A federal law banned Chinese astronauts from the ISS.
beats.visual: photograph of the International Space Station orbiting Earth, 2021

beats.text: That exclusion only forced a rival laboratory into the sky.
beats.visual: illustration of the modular Tiangong space station in Earth orbit, 2021

beats.text: China launched the massive Tianhe core module in 2021.
beats.visual: photograph of the Long March 5B rocket launching the Tianhe core module, 2021
queries: Long March 5B launch Tianhe core module

beats.text: They docked two giant experiment modules to complete the station.
beats.visual: rendering of Wentian and Mengtian modules attached to the Tiangong core, 2022

beats.text: Seventeen different countries now conduct research on this forbidden outpost.
beats.visual: artist concept of scientific experiment racks inside the Tiangong space station, 2022

beats.text: European astronauts even joined their crew for deep-sea survival training.
beats.visual: photograph of European Space Agency astronaut Samantha Cristoforetti during sea survival training, 2017
queries: Samantha Cristoforetti sea survival training China
Matthias Maurer sea survival training China

beats.text: Their new telescope dwarfs Hubble with a field of view 300 times wider.
beats.visual: artist concept of the Xuntian space telescope docking with the Tiangong space station
queries: CSST Chinese space station telescope illustration

beats.text: This rival program was born because of that federal law.
beats.visual: illustration of the completed Tiangong space station orbiting Earth

better_than_last: Enhanced the payoff by framing the telescope as a direct competitive leap and highlighting the ban as the primary catalyst for the rival program's existence.
